title: Narrative Contagion
body:
**Narrative contagion** is the spread of a story that gives people a reason to expect prices to
keep moving. Shiller's argument is that narratives spread socially in the way an epidemic does,
and that demand rises as the story spreads.

The report treats it as distinct from [[Herd Behavior]]. Herding is following what others
do, and contagion is adopting why they say they are doing it, which is more durable, because a
story survives a price drop and supplies a reason to hold.

```
innovation      this technology changes everything
disruption      the incumbent is finished
adoption        everyone will own this eventually
revenge         the institutions had this coming
scarcity        there will never be more of it
```

Each supplies an explanation for a rise that requires no financial statement, which is
precisely what makes it effective on assets that have none.

The fintech connection is speed. A narrative that once spread through newspapers and word of
mouth now moves through a feed in hours, and platforms distribute it and do more than report
it, which is the report's core claim about what has changed.

[[Social Media Dynamics]] in [[INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND SOCIETY]]
describes the amplification mechanism from the other side, where a system optimising engagement
promotes whatever provokes the strongest reaction.
